blocks.title: Family and community
blocks.md: A **family** is a group of people who live together and care for each other: parents, children, grandparents and sometimes aunts, uncles and cousins. A **community** is a group of people who live in the same place (a village or town) and share things like a market, a school and a health centre. Many communities together make a **region**, and all the regions make the **country**.

blocks.caption: From family to region.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: family with parents and children; school with teachers and pupils; village or town with neighbours; region with many towns.

blocks.title: Community helpers
blocks.md: **Teachers** educate us. **Nurses and doctors** care for the sick. **Farmers** grow our food. **Drivers** carry people and goods. **Police officers** keep us safe. **Traders** sell goods in the market. **Chiefs and mayors** help to lead the community. Each person's work is important and we must respect it.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that only adults can help the community: children can keep the school clean, help neighbours and be polite.
- Looking down on a helper because of the kind of work he or she does.
- Forgetting that every member of the family has duties as well as rights.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Who helps you when you are ill, and who teaches you at school?
steps: A nurse or a doctor helps when we are ill.
A teacher teaches us at school.
blocks.answer: a nurse or doctor; a teacher.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Give two ways in which a pupil can help the school community.
steps: Keep the classroom clean and help a classmate who needs help.
blocks.answer: Keep the classroom clean; help a classmate.
